root_cause.text: The IPv4 IP options handling in `ip_options_get()` allowed unprivileged users to set source-routing options (`IPOPT_SSRR`/`IPOPT_LSRR`) because it did not enforce a `CAP_NET_RAW` capability check when `opt->opt.srr` was present.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (opt->opt.srr && !ns_capable(net->user_ns, CAP_NET_RAW)) { ... return -EPERM; }` in `net/ipv4/ip_options.c`, and the CVE/commit message states this is needed to stop unprivileged applications from forcing packets through attacker-controlled nodes and leaking TCP ISN/protocol information.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject source-route IP options in ip_options_get() unless the caller has CAP_NET_RAW in the target network namespace.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added in ip_options_get() after the existing validation path: if opt->opt.srr is set and the caller is not ns_capable(net->user_ns, CAP_NET_RAW), the function now frees the newly allocated opt structure and returns -EPERM before replacing *optp.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents unprivileged callers in the network namespace from successfully setting IP options that include source route recording (srr). Instead of accepting and installing those options, the function now rejects the request with a permission error and avoids updating the stored options.

grouping_result.intent: Reject source-route IP options in ip_options_get() unless the caller has CAP_NET_RAW in the target network namespace.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by adding the missing CAP_NET_RAW check in ip_options_get() when source-route options (SSRR/LSRR via opt->opt.srr) are present.

candidates.rationale: This assigns and accepts the parsed IP options without any capability check after validation, allowing source-routing options present in opt->opt.srr to be installed by unprivileged callers.
This successful return path is reached without enforcing CAP_NET_RAW for source-route options, directly embodying the missing authorization check described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement installs the parsed IP options structure as accepted output without checking whether source-routing options are present in opt->opt.srr and whether the caller has CAP_NET_RAW, which is the core missing authorization described in the root cause.
This success return completes ip_options_get() on the path where source-routing options may have been accepted without a CAP_NET_RAW check, making the unauthorized acceptance effective.

bic_trace_step.reason:
The provided function body for `ip_options_get()` is sufficient because it shows the full call path relevant to the root cause: user-supplied options are copied in, compiled, and accepted. In `ip_options_get()`, after copying user data and setting `opt->is_setbyuser = 1`, the code only does `if (optlen && ip_options_compile(opt, NULL)) { ... return -EINVAL; }` and then accepts the options. There is no check here for `opt->opt.srr`/`opt->srr` and no `capable(CAP_NET_RAW)` enforcement after compilation.

The vulnerable construct is present because `ip_options_compile(opt, NULL)` parses source routing options and explicitly accepts `IPOPT_SSRR` / `IPOPT_LSRR`: in the `case IPOPT_SSRR:` / `case IPOPT_LSRR:` block it validates format, sets `opt->is_strictroute` and `opt->srr = optptr - iph`, but performs no capability check for source-routing options when `!skb`. The only capability checks in `ip_options_compile()` are for malformed/default timestamp mode handling (`default:` inside `IPOPT_TIMESTAMP`) and for `IPOPT_SEC`, `IPOPT_SID`, and other default options (`case IPOPT_SEC: case IPOPT_SID: default:`), via `if (!skb && !capable(CAP_NET_RAW))`. No equivalent check exists in the SSRR/LSRR case.

Therefore unprivileged users can supply source-routing options through `ip_options_get()` and have them accepted, matching the stated root cause. Since the fix would require rejecting compiled options with source routing unless `CAP_NET_RAW` is present, and that logic is absent, this function has the bug and is not fixed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in `ip_options_get()` together with the validation path in `ip_options_compile()`. In `ip_options_get()`, user-supplied options are accepted, `opt->is_setbyuser = 1`, and then validated only by `if (optlen && ip_options_compile(opt, NULL))`. There is no explicit capability check after compilation for source routing. In `ip_options_compile()`, the `case IPOPT_SSRR:` / `case IPOPT_LSRR:` block parses and accepts source-route options, sets `opt->is_strictroute` and `opt->srr = optptr - iph;`, but contains no `capable(CAP_NET_RAW)` check for this case when `!skb`. By contrast, capability checks do exist for other options, e.g. `default:` under timestamp handling and the generic `case IPOPT_SEC: case IPOPT_SID: default:` path both do `if (!skb && !capable(CAP_NET_RAW)) ... goto error;`. Because source-routing options are specifically accepted without such a privilege check, unprivileged users can set `IPOPT_SSRR`/`IPOPT_LSRR`. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not present.
